items.witness_reading: The closed-immersion quotient, the extension identity J O_(S,fr_S)=J^p, and the equality J=J^p all print an ordinary-looking superscript p. No separate bracketed Frobenius-power definition is supplied in these passages.
items.mathematical_resolution: The only mathematically valid reading here is the ideal generated by p-th powers of local sections of J, often denoted J^[p], not the ordinary product power. On an affine open, base change by Frobenius sends A/J to A/(a^p:a∈J). For A=F_2[x,y], J=(x,y), the generated ideal is (x^2,y^2), whereas the ordinary square also contains xy. The Nakayama argument remains valid: for a proper ideal in a local ring, J^[p]⊂mJ; J=J^[p] with J finitely generated forces J=0. This resolves the meaning, without claiming the original author explicitly defined a special notation.
items.proposed_correction: Retain original $\JJ^p$ throughout; add the visible notation explanation to the separate 校勘说明 appendix. No mathematical-text patch proposed.

items.witness_reading: The auxiliary lifting claim on printed478 assumes Q_0 projective and an arbitrary A-module R with T(R)≅R_0; it does not print flatness of R. Printed477 has just shown all cycles Z_0^i are projective.
items.mathematical_resolution: The auxiliary claim is false for arbitrary R because tensoring the short exact sequence need not preserve left exactness. Counterexample: A=Z/4, I=(2), A_0=F_2, S_0=(0→0→F_2→F_2→0), R=F_2. Any projective lift Q of Q_0=F_2 is Z/4; its surjection to R has kernel F_2, whose reduction is nonzero, contradicting P_0=0. Adding R flat makes Tor_1^A(A_0,R)=0 and repairs exactness. In the actual descending construction R_0=Z_0^{i+1} is projective, so choose a projective (hence flat) lift R by Lemma3(ii); thus the corollary and subsequent lemma proofs remain valid.
items.proposed_correction: In this auxiliary claim, use the projectivity of R0 already proved in the descending induction, and choose its projective lift R by Lemma3(ii); append the splitting justification. The exact two patches below are a visible, mathematically justified repair of the original auxiliary argument, with the accompanying appendix note explaining the original missing flatness.
